facts.text: The Sargasso Sea is the only sea whose boundaries are entirely ocean currents
About 40 gallons of maple sap are needed to make one gallon of syrup
Velcro began after George de Mestral studied burrs clinging to clothes and dog fur
Lake Baikal holds about 20% of the world's unfrozen freshwater reserve
Will Kellogg's accidental wheat flakes led him to develop corn flakes with his brother
Limpet teeth have the highest recorded tensile strength for a biological material

cta: Enjoyed these facts? Like the video and follow for more!
caption: Curiosity gets better when every fact comes from somewhere unexpected.

quality_rationales.opening_strength: The Sargasso Sea opens with an immediate geographic reversal that is easy to picture and explain.
quality_rationales.surprise_quality: Five facts are strength 2 and the six facts span four controlled surprise-operator families without exceeding the repetition limits.
quality_rationales.concrete_detail: The post uses ocean-current boundaries, a 40-to-1 production ratio, invention mechanisms, a 20-percent freshwater share, and a measured material record.
quality_rationales.shareability: The cross-topic mix gives several short tell-someone facts with distinct visual, historical, geographic, and numerical payoffs.
quality_rationales.readability: All six visible facts contain one main idea in 11 to 14 words and preserve the qualifiers needed for accuracy.
quality_rationales.factual_confidence: Every selected claim is supported by an opened NOAA, UNESCO, Cornell, MIT, or peer-reviewed university source with matching scope.

weakest_fact_review.reason: The corn-flakes origin is less visually strong than the others but adds a familiar food connection and a distinct historical payoff.
The maple-syrup ratio is straightforward but remains unusually concrete, memorable, and strongly sourced.
